findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Specify WHERE in compose-up.sh the daemon.json merge is inserted (ahead of `systemctl enable --now docker` at line 55) and how an already-running daemon is reloaded/restarted so the merged builder.gc policy is actually loaded on an idempotent re-run.
evidence: Plan: "`compose-up.sh` installs it before starting Docker."
compose-up.sh:55 `systemctl enable --now docker` is the first side-effecting step, preceding all materialize-* config steps
search for 'daemon.json' in compose-up.sh returned (no matches) — no existing seam to merge into
compose-up.sh header claims idempotent/safe-to-re-run: a merge on an already-running daemon has no effect without a reload/restart
findings.finding: The plan asserts compose-up.sh 'installs it before starting Docker', but in the current compose-up.sh the FIRST side-effecting step is `systemctl enable --now docker` (line 55), and every config/materialize step runs after Docker is already started; there is no existing daemon.json handling to extend. The daemon.json merge must therefore be inserted ahead of line 55, and an idempotent re-run against an already-running daemon needs an explicit reload/restart to apply the merged builder.gc policy.
findings.location: Design → 'The cap is enforced by Docker's OWN GC' / AC line 'installed by compose-up.sh'; infra/scripts/compose-up.sh:55
scenarios: Re-running compose-up.sh on a box whose Docker daemon is already up: the merged builder.gc policy is written but never loaded, so the cap silently does not take effect
A daemon.json merge inserted after line 55 would start Docker before the GC policy exists, contradicting the plan's own 'before starting Docker' requirement
findings.suggested_fix: Insert the daemon.json merge before line 55, and after the merge conditionally `systemctl reload docker || systemctl restart docker` when the policy changed, so both first-boot and re-run apply the cap to a live daemon.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Pin (or probe) the target Docker engine version and verify the exact `builder.gc` config surface against that engine's `dockerd`/daemon.json schema (confirm `defaultKeepStorage` vs the newer `builder.gc.policy` reservedSpace/maxUsedSpace/minFreeSpace keys), and state the verified keys in the plan.
evidence: Plan quote: "renders the daemon's native BuildKit GC policy (`builder.gc`, `defaultKeepStorage` plus a policy list) into `/etc/docker/daemon.json`"
No engine-version pin: compose-up.sh installs Docker via `dnf install -y docker` (infra/scripts/compose-up.sh:53) with no version constraint; the effective daemon.json GC schema is version-sensitive.

Evidence class: Partially-verified — `builder.gc` config exists as a Docker daemon capability, but the specific `defaultKeepStorage` key's continued support on the target engine is UNVERIFIED and version-dependent.
findings.finding: The plan asserts the daemon-native BuildKit GC config (`builder.gc`, `defaultKeepStorage`, policy list) merged into /etc/docker/daemon.json will enforce the 5 GiB BuildKit cap, but names `defaultKeepStorage` by exact key without pinning the target Docker engine version — a key Docker deprecated in newer engines in favor of `builder.gc.policy` reservedSpace/maxUsedSpace/minFreeSpace. On the AL2023 `dnf install docker` engine the rendered key could be ignored, silently defeating the source-of-truth cap.
findings.location: Design §'The cap is enforced by Docker's OWN GC, at the source'; AC line 2 (BuildKit cap enforced by builder.gc)
scenarios: compose-up.sh installs a Docker engine where `defaultKeepStorage` is deprecated/renamed; the daemon accepts the file but ignores the key, so BuildKit cache grows unbounded despite the cap being 'installed'.
daemon.json contains a key the engine rejects, and dockerd fails to (re)start after the merge.
findings.suggested_fix: Add a Design note pinning the AL2023 Docker engine version and citing its daemon.json builder.gc schema; if the engine is Docker 26+, render `builder.gc.policy` with reservedSpace/maxUsedSpace and treat `defaultKeepStorage` as the legacy fallback only. Have the daemon.json test assert the rendered keys match the pinned engine's accepted schema.

evidence: 2 criterion line(s) bundle multiple deliverables with 'and' (split so each is independently verifiable).
findings.suggested_fix: Split compound criteria, replace subjective terms with observable outcomes, and state how each is verified.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Tighten the Design prose so 'enforced by Docker's OWN GC' is scoped to the 5 GiB BuildKit share only, and state explicitly that the 15 GiB image/layer share is enforced by autodeploy prune while the unaccounted overlay2 mass is alarm-only (unenforceable by cap or prune).
evidence: Plan: 'renders the daemon's native BuildKit GC policy (builder.gc, defaultKeepStorage plus a policy list) ... so the daemon refuses growth on its own schedule'
Plan elsewhere concedes the orphan mass 'is the one quantity no cap and no prune can reach', and AC2 correctly narrows daemon enforcement to 'The BuildKit cap'
autodeploy.sh:377 shows the image/layer share is actually enforced by `docker builder prune --keep-storage` + `docker image prune`, i.e. an external sweeper, not the daemon
findings.finding: The Design section overstates what the daemon's native GC enforces: `builder.gc`/`defaultKeepStorage` bound only the BuildKit build cache, not overlay2 image layers and not the orphaned overlay2 mass the outage was about — yet the prose reads as if the daemon enforces the whole 20 GiB budget 'at the source'.
findings.location: Design > 'The cap is enforced by Docker's OWN GC, at the source'
scenarios: Implementer reads the Design prose and expects the merged daemon.json to bound the 15 GiB image share or the unaccounted overlay2, then finds builder.gc only touches BuildKit cache

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Add a daemon.json validity check (and backup/rollback) before restarting Docker, so a bad merge cannot leave dockerd unable to start.
evidence: 'renders ... into /etc/docker/daemon.json by JSON MERGE'
'compose-up.sh installs it before starting Docker'
Absence: no daemon.json backup, no pre-restart validity check, no rollback if dockerd fails to start
findings.finding: The plan merges a BuildKit GC policy into /etc/docker/daemon.json and installs it before starting Docker, but specifies no validation-before-restart or backout if the merge produces a daemon.json the daemon rejects — a malformed daemon.json prevents dockerd from starting, which is a self-inflicted outage on the very host the plan is protecting.
findings.location: Design — 'The cap is enforced by Docker's OWN GC' / AC line 2
findings.suggested_fix: State that the script writes to a temp file, validates JSON (and ideally `dockerd --validate` or equivalent), keeps the prior daemon.json as a backup, and restores it if the daemon fails to come up.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Pin the target Docker Engine version and confirm its `builder.gc` schema (defaultKeepStorage vs reservedSpace/maxUsedSpace/minFreeSpace), rendering the keys the running daemon actually honors.
evidence: Plan: 'renders the daemon's native BuildKit GC policy (`builder.gc`, `defaultKeepStorage` plus a policy list)'
Docker Docs 'Build garbage collection' documents current builder.gc config keys
moby/moby issue #46864 (Nov 2023): 'BuildKit gc config is complicated, and doesn't allow for multiple filters in daemon.json' — shows defaultKeepStorage + policy list is finicky and version-dependent
Newer Docker Engine replaced defaultKeepStorage with reservedSpace/maxUsedSpace/minFreeSpace
findings.finding: The plan hard-codes BuildKit `defaultKeepStorage` as the daemon GC cap key, an unverified capability assertion: recent Docker Engine versions deprecate `defaultKeepStorage` in favor of `reservedSpace`/`maxUsedSpace`/`minFreeSpace` under `builder.gc`, and the daemon.json GC schema is documented as version-sensitive and error-prone.
findings.location: Design → 'The cap is enforced by Docker's OWN GC, at the source' / AC line 2 (builder.gc policy)
scenarios: Target host runs a Docker Engine version where defaultKeepStorage is deprecated/ignored, so the rendered daemon.json silently fails to cap BuildKit
findings.suggested_fix: State the minimum Docker Engine version the daemon.json render targets and, if it is Engine 28+, use `reservedSpace`/`maxUsedSpace` (or emit both key families guarded by version detection) rather than only the older `defaultKeepStorage`.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Resolve the du-on-overlay2 accuracy assumption — document that du over overlay2 is directional (lowerdir/merged/whiteout overhead), and justify the 2 GiB threshold against expected normal-state divergence.
evidence: Plan: 'one `du` invocation, so overlay2's hardlinks are counted once' and 'overlay2 truth minus the ledger, clamped at 0. That delta IS the orphan mass'
Netdata guide: 'du can double-count overlay2 layers because stacked overlay mounts include lowerdir data, so treat overlay2/ numbers as directional, not exact'
Dash0 FAQ: 'Docker counts layers logically; the filesystem counts the bytes overlay2 actually uses, including whiteout files and merged directory overhead ... diverging by a few hundred MB is normal'
findings.finding: The plan claims a single `du -s` over overlay2 yields 'filesystem truth' with hardlinks 'counted once', but overlay2 du is widely documented as directional (stacked overlay lowerdir/merged overhead, whiteouts), so the accuracy assertion underpinning `docker_unaccounted_bytes` is unverified.
findings.location: Design → 'Detecting the bytes docker system df cannot see' / metric docker_unaccounted_bytes
scenarios: Normal-state overlay2 du/df divergence (documented as up to hundreds of MB) sits below the 2 GiB unaccounted alarm, or stacked-mount overhead inflates the delta into a false positive

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] State the du walk's timeout/cost bound (and its expected duration on a large overlay2) so the 5-min probe cannot become a self-inflicted I/O load or a chronic false-page source.
evidence: 'du -s over /var/lib/docker and /var/lib/docker/overlay2 (one du invocation ...)'
'5-min probe' with 'failed/timed-out probe publishes NOTHING'
findings.finding: The filesystem-truth measurement runs `du -s` over the whole /var/lib/docker and overlay2 tree on a 5-minute probe, but the plan states no I/O cost bound for that walk on a busy host with a large layer set (17G / 67 layer dirs at the incident); du walks every inode and can be slow, contending with the daemon it measures.
findings.location: Design — 'Detecting the bytes docker system df cannot see' / Metrics '5-min probe'
findings.suggested_fix: Document a probe timeout and its relationship to the 300s period, and note the expected du runtime envelope (or an ionice/one-shot mitigation) for a large /var/lib/docker.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] State an explicit, cheap rollback for the daemon.json builder.gc injection (e.g. a backup of the prior daemon.json and a documented restore + daemon-reload step) and note whether the daemon reconfiguration is applied in a single flip or observed before relying on it.
evidence: 'renders the daemon's native BuildKit GC policy ... into /etc/docker/daemon.json by JSON MERGE, so the daemon refuses growth on its own schedule'
'compose-up.sh installs it before starting Docker'
ABSENCE: no stated way to revert the builder.gc injection or roll back to the prior daemon.json if the new GC ceiling proves wrong in production
findings.finding: The plan installs a native BuildKit GC policy into /etc/docker/daemon.json via compose-up.sh — a runtime behavior change to a long-running Docker daemon — but states no rollback path if the daemon GC misbehaves (e.g. reclaims cache too aggressively and slows builds, or a merged policy interacts badly with pre-existing daemon config). The idempotent-merge property covers re-install, not undo.
findings.location: Design — 'The cap is enforced by Docker's OWN GC, at the source' / AC: 'The BuildKit cap is enforced by the daemon's own builder.gc policy, merged idempotently'
scenarios: A too-low defaultKeepStorage evicts warm BuildKit cache, builds slow dramatically, and operators have no documented one-step revert to the pre-cap daemon.json
findings.suggested_fix: Add an AC/runbook step: compose-up.sh backs up the prior daemon.json before merge, and the runbook documents restoring it and reloading the daemon to revert the GC policy.
